question: Should OpenClaw adopt this taxonomy-wide evidence-ownership rebaseline, including reducing `smoke-ci` from 30 claimed categories to the 10 categories exercised by its fixed plan?
rationale: The code can enforce the selected invariant, but whether the narrowed profile is the intended release-signal contract is a maintainer QA-policy decision rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Approve the rebaseline after final CI
options.body: Accept catalog-owned atomic coverage IDs and the narrower smoke profile once maintainers confirm the 10 categories are the intended smoke contract and the failed checks are cleared or explained.

options.title: Keep broader smoke accounting
options.body: Ask for a revised taxonomy/catalog mapping that preserves the former smoke-category scope or adds executable scenarios for the removed categories.

options.title: Split profile policy from the ID cleanup
options.body: Land only the mechanically validated ID-ownership normalization in a narrower follow-up and decide smoke-profile semantics separately.

recommendation.title: Approve the rebaseline after final CI
recommendation.body: Accept catalog-owned atomic coverage IDs and the narrower smoke profile once maintainers confirm the 10 categories are the intended smoke contract and the failed checks are cleared or explained.
